conf_rule: with the enabled reference stack, /etc/security/pwhistory.conf and the vendor fallback /usr/etc/security/pwhistory.conf must each be absent or have no active line (as pam_modutil_search_key reads them: '#' starts a comment, leading whitespace is skipped, an empty line is inactive); an active line is ERROR pwhistory-conf:active-lines, a non-regular file is ERROR
error_value_contract: Every ERROR wire value is a stable <domain>:<reason> code.
module_rule: only reference password stacks of /etc/pam.d/common-password are accepted, compared word by word over the active password lines (user decision 27.09.2026, confirmed by the logs of all seven supported environments): clean install (pam_unix obscure yescrypt, pam_deny, pam_permit) and the stack after APPLY 1.1 (requisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3, pam_unix obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt, pam_deny, pam_permit) are VALUE <module-absent> FAIL; the same stack with requisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=5 retry=1 use_authtok between pam_pwquality and pam_unix is the enabled stack; any other stack, a line continuation, an @include line or a NUL byte is ERROR
source_rule: fstec-configuration-2026 1.2 requires preventing password reuse by keeping a history of used passwords per the password policy; 1.1 table 1 names a history of at least 5-10; value by user decision 26.09.2026: pam_pwhistory remember at least 5
value_rule: VALUE of the enabled reference stack is 5, the remember argument of its pam_pwhistory line; the explicit arguments remember=5 and retry=1 override pwhistory.conf in Linux-PAM 1.4.0-1.7.x
